results.title: a client-supplied cf-connecting-ip is refused at the edge, not silently overwritten
results.detail: RPC returning request.headers with the anon key. No client header -> 200, cf-connecting-ip present (true), x-forwarded-for carried 1 address(es), and cf-connecting-ip equalled its sole element (true). Same call carrying cf-connecting-ip=203.0.113.9 -> 403: the edge REFUSES the request rather than overwriting the header, so the forged value never reaches SQL (true). Addresses deliberately not recorded.

results.title: the hdr.ip() expression admits a forged caller; the cf-connecting-ip form does not
results.detail: Allowlist contains only 203.0.113.9. One request, carrying x-forwarded-for=203.0.113.9, against two tables whose policies differ only in which header they read. Keyed on cf-connecting-ip -> 200, 0 row(s): the forged value is not what the edge set, so the policy denies. Keyed on split_part(x-forwarded-for, ',', 1) - the hdr.ip() body - to 200, 1 row(s): the caller chose an address in the allowlist and the policy admitted them.

results.title: a zero-arg IMMUTABLE function reading request.headers is evaluated at plan time
results.detail: Same body, same qual, two volatility classes. IMMUTABLE: the plan is a constant One-Time Filter with no current_setting call left in it (true) - the planner evaluated the header read once and baked the answer in, dropping the scan. STABLE: the GUC read survives into the plan and runs per execution (true). pg_headerkit marks in_allow_list()/in_deny_list() IMMUTABLE and both take zero arguments, so a policy written with them is a plan-time constant rather than a per-request check.

results.title: the platform security advisor and extension-owned objects
results.detail: pg_tle available; installed a slice of pg_headerkit as a real extension (two unpinned-search_path functions + an RLS-less table in schema hdr). Advisor lints before: 8, after: 9; lints added: extension_in_publicx1; any lint naming an hdr object: false. Same-run control - this module's own plain-SQL objects of the same two shapes are named by: anon_security_definer_function_executable,authenticated_security_definer_function_executable,extension_in_public,function_search_path_mutable,rls_disabled_in_public. The advisor raises those lints for plain SQL and not for the extension's objects in the SAME response, so extension membership is the difference and a customer installing a dbdev package gets no advisor coverage of what it brought in.
